findings.title: Account UI error uses Java MessageFormat instead of i18next placeholders
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from i18next placeholders (Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).) to Java MessageFormat, including a ChoiceFormat subpattern: Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. Every other string in this account-ui bundle uses {{name}} / {{0}} (and <0> Trans tags), and apostrophes are not doubled the way MessageFormat requires, so this file is not formatted by Java. i18next will not substitute {0}/{1}/{2} and will not evaluate {2,choice,...}. Users who hit the multivalued-size validator will see the raw format string, including the < in 1<values, instead of the attribute name and limits. The previous {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} wording did not need this change to satisfy the new HTML check.

findings.title: Admin UI error uses Java MessageFormat instead of i18next placeholders
findings.body: The same key in the React admin-ui bundle was rewritten from Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s). to Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. That bundle is loaded by i18next (the previous value already used {{0}} interpolation). i18next will leave {0}, {1}, {2}, and the Java choice pattern as literal text, so administrators validating a multivalued user-profile attribute see an uninterpolated format string rather than the attribute name and min/max. ChoiceFormat is not an i18next plural form; keep the {{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}} placeholders (for example the old value(s) wording).

findings.title: Choice-format pre-strip bypasses the HTML sanitizer
findings.body: Before the OWASP policy runs, normalizeValue deletes every {n,choice,...} substring for error-invalid-multivalued-size and any key starting with linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit. Anything inside that substring, including tags, is never sanitized. A community translation can therefore ship active HTML such as {0,choice,0#<a href="https://evil.example">click|1#minute} and the new check will still pass. linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.* values are interpolated into HTML emails, and error-invalid-multivalued-size is shown in the account and admin UIs, so this bypasses the control the PR adds. Replace only the ChoiceFormat limit marker (the N< in 1<values) or reject choice subformats that contain tags, instead of discarding the whole pattern before sanitize().

findings.title: Lithuanian account totpStep1 replaced with Italian
findings.body: totpStep1 was rewritten to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The surrounding strings in this file are Lithuanian (for example totpStep2 is still "Atidarykite programėlę..."). Lithuanian users setting up an authenticator in the account theme will be shown Italian instructions. This looks like a copy-paste from the Italian bundle when the old FreeOTP/Google Play anchors were removed.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" while the rest of this login bundle remains Lithuanian (loginTotpStep2 is still "Atidarykite programėlę ir nuskenuokite barkodą..."). Lithuanian users on the OTP setup page will get Italian text. The HTML links needed to be removed to match the English source, but the replacement string is the wrong language.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese totpStep1 written in Traditional Chinese
findings.body: totpStep1 was set to "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式). This is the zh_CN bundle: the previous line is Simplified 手机, and totpStep2 is Simplified 打开应用. Simplified Chinese users configuring OTP in the account theme will see Traditional script mixed into an otherwise Simplified flow. A Simplified rendering of the same sentence would use 手机/安装/应用程序 (the zh_CN login bundle already uses Simplified for the equivalent loginTotpStep1).
